period.label: Eres Luz era / female cante × pop (late 1990s–2000s)

position_in_era.primary_genre_lineage: flamenco cante × pop / rumba (mainstream female-cante crossover)
position_in_era.geographic_locus: San Fernando, Cádiz (same town as Camarón)
position_in_era.historical_role: Same-era lateral peer in the female-cante translation lineage. Born 1978 in San Fernando — Camarón's home town — and personally mentored by Camarón as a child. Worked with Alejandro Sanz and Paco Ortega on her first three albums; commercially the most-heard female cante voice of the late 1990s and 2000s. Pop-leaning crossover, a gentler lateral on the female-voice translation axis.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Debut *Entre dos puertos* (1996), produced with Alejandro Sanz and Paco Ortega, sold 150,000+; *Eres luz* (1998) extended the formula.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Mentored by Camarón directly; Alejandro Sanz and Paco Ortega as production partners.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: San Fernando, Cádiz — exact same flamenco town as Camarón.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Cante over flamenco guitar plus pop band instrumentation.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: Multiple Latin Grammy wins through the 2000s; sustained mainstream Spanish-radio presence.
